Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on authentication and key management so your engineering team can validate integration impact: 

Call recap (high-level)
- Use case: server-side API calls to Redwood for generation, embeddings, and reranking from FintechCo backend and batch jobs.
- Security goals: short-lived credentials, strict scoping per-route, rotation policy, and auditability for SOC-type controls.
- Primary ask today: confirm recommended auth flows (API keys vs service accounts/OAuth/JWT), rotation strategy, and SDK support for automatic token refresh.

Action items / next steps
1) We’ll send a short technical note covering recommended patterns (API keys for quick start, service accounts + JWT for prod, rotation APIs, scopes) — owner: Dev Patel (see attached dev-answers).
2) We'll include an integration checklist and a sample service account JSON + SDK snippet for rotation demo — owner: Marissa.
3) Schedule a 30m follow-up demo for your infra and security teams to walk through rotation and scoping in the SDK. Please propose slots next week.

Attachments: redwood-authn-overview.pdf, integration-checklist.xlsx

A few clarifying questions for your engineers so we can tailor the note: 
- Do you prefer a service-account / JWT approach (server-to-server) or do you need user-scoped OAuth flows for any client-side features?
- Any corporate restrictions on long-lived static credentials (e.g., disallow static API keys)?
- Do you need audit log export (S3/BigQuery) for token events?

I'll let Dev take the technical answers below. Thanks — looking forward to the follow-up.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa, thanks for the summary — very helpful. A few answers and follow-ups from our side: 

- For server-to-server calls, we prefer service accounts with short-lived tokens (no long-lived static keys for prod). We can do API keys for dev/staging but they'd be locked down.
- Audit logs: yes, we need logs forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk). Ideally token issue/revoke events and API key creation are exported.
- Scoping: we need per-route scopes so embeddings-only keys can't call generation and vice versa.

Technical Qs for Dev: 
1) What token TTLs do you recommend for service accounts?
2) Do you provide an admin endpoint / UI to rotate/revoke keys, and is rotation auditable?
3) Can the SDK automatically refresh tokens using a service account private key?
4) Any IP allowlist options for dedicated endpoints?

We can do a follow-up demo. Availability next Tue/Wed 10–12 PT or Thu 13–15 PT.

—Alex

Hi Alex — great questions. Short answers below plus references to attached dev-answers doc for full examples.

1) Recommended token TTLs
- Service account JWTs: exchange for short-lived access tokens (recommended TTL 15–60 minutes).
- Long-lived API keys: allowed for non-prod; rotate every 30 days if used.

2) Rotation & admin UI
- Yes: Redwood offers both an Admin UI (Console) and an Admin REST API for key lifecycle: create, list, rotate, revoke. All actions are audited and available via the Audit Log export (S3/GCS/BigQuery).
- Rotation options: manual rotate, scheduled rolling rotation (recommended for teams using static keys), and immediate revoke on compromise.

3) SDK refresh support
- Official Redwood SDKs (Node, Python, Java) include built-in helpers to do JWT-based service account exchange and automatic token refresh. Typical flow: service_account.json (private key) -> local JWT -> exchange at /v1/auth/token -> SDK caches token and refreshes before expiry.
- Sample snippet included in dev-answers (dev-answers-rotation-snippet).

4) IP allowlist & scoping
- Dedicated / private deployments: support per-tenant IP allowlists at the route level. For hosted API, we provide CIDR allowlist options for API keys and signed JWT audiences.
- Scopes: you can create scoped API keys/service-account roles: embeddings.read, embeddings.write, generation.chat, rerank.execute, admin.keys. We recommend issuing least-privilege credentials per service.

Additional notes
- Embeddings & reranking: restrict to embeddings.* and rerank.execute scopes. If you plan to use rerankers as a backend service, create a service account bound to that microservice and limit network access.
- Audit/event collection: token issuance, rotation, and revoke events are logged and can be pushed to your SIEM; we can provide a sample sink config for Splunk.

Attachments: dev-answers-20270430.md (contains endpoint paths, sample request/response, and SDK snippets), sample-service-account.json (redacted).

If helpful, we can run a short demo showing creating a service account, doing the JWT exchange, and showing rotation via the Admin API + SDK. Marissa, can we lock a slot during Alex's proposed times?

Thanks,
Dev
